Project Manager – Large Projects Administrative Project Management Focus Position Summary The Project Manager – Large Projects is responsible for the administrative coordination, governance, documentation, tracking, and reporting required to support large, complex projects.

This role ensures that project information is organized, timelines are visible, actions are tracked, risks and issues are documented, and stakeholders have accurate information to support decision-making. This role does not own solution design, deployment strategy, customer adoption, operational readiness, or business execution.

Instead, the Project Manager provides the structure, cadence, documentation, and administrative discipline needed to keep large projects organized and transparent.

This is an individual contributor role that works closely with project sponsors, workstream owners, Solution Deployment Leaders, commercial teams, operations, finance, legal, quality, supply chain, digital, and other stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities: Project Administration and Coordination Maintain project plans, timelines, milestones, action trackers, decision logs, risk logs, issue logs, and dependency trackers. Coordinate project meetings, governance forums, steering committee reviews, and stakeholder update sessions.

Prepare meeting agendas, capture minutes, document decisions, and follow up on assigned actions. Ensure project documentation is complete, current, organized, and accessible to appropriate stakeholders. Support consistent use of project templates, tools, trackers, and reporting formats.

Governance Support Support project governance by maintaining meeting cadence, escalation records, approval documentation, and decision history. Track required approvals, sign-offs, stage gates, and governance checkpoints. Ensure project sponsors and workstream owners have accurate information for reviews and decisions.

Maintain visibility to open decisions, overdue actions, unresolved issues, and upcoming milestones. Help ensure governance processes are followed consistently across large projects. Timeline and Milestone Tracking Maintain the master project timeline based on input from workstream owners and accountable business leads.

Track progress against milestones, deliverables, and agreed due dates. Identify and flag timeline variances, overdue items, and dependency gaps for review by accountable owners. Consolidate updates from multiple workstreams into a single project view. Support visibility to critical path items without owning execution of the underlying work.

Reporting and Communication Support Prepare project status reports, dashboards, executive summaries, and stakeholder updates. Consolidate inputs from workstream owners, deployment leaders, finance, operations, commercial teams, and other functions.

Ensure project reports clearly reflect status, milestones, risks, issues, decisions needed, and next steps. Maintain accurate records of project communications and leadership updates. Support consistent and timely information flow across project stakeholders. Risk, Issue, and Action Tracking Maintain risk, issue, action, and dependency logs.

Document risk descriptions, issue status, owners, target dates, mitigation updates, and escalation history. Follow up with accountable owners to obtain updates and closure status. Flag overdue actions, unresolved issues, or missing information to project sponsors or designated leads.

Support escalation documentation but does not own resolution of technical, operational, commercial, or deployment issues. Budget and Resource Administration Track project budget information, purchase orders, invoices, resource assumptions, and financial updates as directed by finance or project sponsors.

Consolidate budget and resource inputs for project reporting. Maintain documentation related to project spend, approvals, forecasts, and financial decisions. Support administrative coordination of vendor documentation, contracts, statements of work, and related records.

Flag missing financial information, pending approvals, or budget variances for review by accountable owners. Documentation and Records Management Maintain organized project repositories, files, version control, and document naming standards.

Ensure key project documents, approvals, meeting records, reports, and governance materials are stored appropriately. Support audit readiness by maintaining clear records of decisions, approvals, risks, changes, and status updates. Capture lessons learned and archive project materials at project close.

Support continuous improvement of project administration tools, templates, and documentation practices. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, project management, life sciences, engineering, or related field preferred.

Experience supporting large projects, complex initiatives, project management offices, commercial operations, business operations, or administrative project coordination. Strong skills in project documentation, meeting coordination, status reporting, action tracking, and records management.

Ability to consolidate information from multiple stakeholders into clear, accurate project updates. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple deadlines, documents, trackers, and reporting cycles. Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Proficiency with project management, collaboration, reporting, and productivity tools. Ability to work in a matrixed organization and follow up with stakeholders across functions and levels. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting large customer, commercial, operational, supply chain, digital, or transformation projects.

Experience in life sciences, pharmaceutical, biopharma, healthcare, diagnostics, laboratory, manufacturing, or regulated environments. Familiarity with project governance, PMO practices, stage-gate processes, and executive reporting.

Experience with tools such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams, Power BI, CRM, ERP, or similar platforms. Understanding of budget tracking, purchase order processes, vendor documentation, or contract administration. Project management certification or training preferred but not required.

Key Competencies Project administration Documentation management Meeting coordination Status reporting Timeline tracking Action-item follow-up Risk and issue logging Governance support Records management Attention to detail Stakeholder follow-up Tool and tracker discipline Scope and Impact The Project Manager – Large Projects is an individual contributor role focused on the administrative management of large, complex projects.

The role supports project transparency, governance discipline, documentation quality, leadership visibility, and timely follow-up. The role does not own solution deployment, customer adoption, operational readiness, business execution, technical solution design, or commercial strategy.

Accountability for those activities remains with designated business owners, Solution Deployment Leaders, Solution Architects, commercial leaders, and functional teams. Travel Requirements Limited travel may be required for project meetings, governance sessions, workshops, or site-based coordination.

Compensation and Benefits The salary range estimated for this position based in California is $112,500.00–$168,500.00. This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy.

Clēnera is a tier-one developer and independent power producer located in Boise, Idaho, and is the U.S. subsidiary of Enlight Renewable Energy (Nasdaq: ENLT ). We develop, finance, construct, own, and operate utility-scale solar and energy storage facilities throughout the United States.

In its 2025 analysis of solar independent power producers, S&P Global ranked Clēnera as a top ten U.S. owner of planned installations in the next five years. Clēnera has over 1.9 GW of solar and 5.1 GWh of storage in operations or construction, and a development pipeline totaling 17.8 GW of solar and 51.1 GWh of storage across 23 states.

Our company culture is at the core of everything we do, so you’ll regularly find Caring, Committed, and Courageous individuals who value respectful, cross-functional collaboration with partners internally and externally. With our tremendous portfolio growth, we are increasing our headcount to meet the demands of the business.

Are you ready to change the world with us? ABOUT THE ROLE The HV & Commissioning Project Manager represents the Owner (IPP) and leads all high-voltage (HV), protection & controls (P&C), SCADA/communications, testing, and commissioning activities for utility-scale solar and energy storage assets.

This role owns cost, schedule, scope, quality, and risk for the HV build and commissioning phases from pre-functional checks through energization, interconnection testing, COD, and turnover to Operations.

Functions as the primary interface with utilities, Owner’s engineers, EPCs, testing/commissioning vendors, and internal stakeholders, ensuring systems are safe, compliant, utility-approved, and reliable for long-term operations.

WHAT YOU'LL DO Own end-to-end HV and site wide commissioning project planning and control, establishing the WBS, baseline schedule, cash flow forecasts, procurement milestones, and resource plans. Drive weekly schedule reviews, recovery planning, and critical path management with EPC and site leadership.

Lead HV and site wide commissioning cost management and forecasting, including monthly EAC/EVA updates, change order pricing validation, contingency management, pay application review/approval, and alignment of financial reporting with Project Controls and Finance.

Direct contract administration, ensuring scope clarity, deliverable compliance, and change management discipline; draft, negotiate, and recommend change orders and claims with clear schedule/cost impact analyses.

Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit and that can carry cargo - and potentially humans in the longer run.
Storm is TEC’s high-performance liquid rocket engine program, developed to support next-generation launch and space transportation applications. The Storm development strategy relies heavily on ground testing, from early development models to qualification and acceptance campaigns. The engine test bench is a critical enabler of the program, and its on-time delivery is essential to maintain the Storm development schedule.
As Storm Engine Test Bench Program Manager, you are responsible for driving the on-time delivery of the Storm engine test bench development program.

You will ensure execution discipline across the bench development workstream: integrating schedules, tracking deliverables, coordinating stakeholders and suppliers, anticipating blockers, and escalating decisions to keep the program on track.

In addition, you will act as the primary point of contact for identifying and securing a suitable test bench location, coordinating the site selection process with internal stakeholders and external parties.

Program planning and delivery (schedule, scope, cost tracking)
Build, maintain, and continuously improve the integrated test bench delivery plan (design maturity gates, procurement lead times, manufacturing, installation, integration, and commissioning support activities).
Own the critical path , dependencies, and milestone readiness criteria (from a delivery perspective).
Track progress, identify schedule threats early, and drive recovery plans (re-sequencing, parallelization, expediting, resourcing proposals).
Maintain program routines (weekly reviews, action tracking, decision logs) to ensure execution discipline.
Cross-functional coordination and communication
Animate weekly/monthly routines: bench program reviews, schedule reviews, and interface meetings
Ensure alignment between propulsion engineering, test engineering, facilities/infrastructure, procurement, quality, and site teams
Prepare concise reporting for program leadership: status, risks, mitigation, upcoming decisions, and milestone readiness
Coordinate preparation of key internal reviews (bench concept reviews, design/package readiness, delivery readiness checkpoints)
Test bench location identification and site selection (point of contact)
Act as the single point of contact to identify, assess, and secure a test bench location aligned with the Storm schedule and development needs.
Coordinate the site selection process (timeline, stakeholder alignment, decision gates, and documentation) and ensure decisions are taken in time to protect the critical path.
With support from the engineering team (who define requirements and technical needs), consolidate the test site needs impacting the choice of location and translate them into:
A practical location assessment checklist (capabilities, utilities, access, constraints)
A comparison of candidate sites (schedule, cost, readiness, risks)
Clear decision packages for leadership (trade-offs, recommended option, fallback plans)
Coordinate interfaces with external stakeholders as needed (site operators, landlords/partners, utilities, local service providers), in alignment with internal owners.
Procurement and supplier coordination
Coordinate long-lead procurement tracking
Support supplier selection and onboarding (RFI/RFQ process coordination, delivery tracking, expediting)
Monitor supplier performance and ensure timely resolution of delivery issues, NCR handling coordination, and logistics readiness
Ensure documentation deliverables from suppliers are collected and integrated
Integration and commissioning readiness support
Ensure prerequisites for integration/commissioning are planned and tracked: procedures availability, resources, tooling, spares, training needs and documentation readiness (owned by responsible teams)
Track open points, coordinate closure plans, and ensure readiness evidence is available for management decisions.
Support lessons-learned capture and incorporation into the next iterations of bench capability

Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or similar
Significant experience delivering complex test infrastructure or propulsion tests programs
Proven program management experience (planning, budgeting, risk, suppliers)
Strong understanding of propulsion testing, cryogenic systems, and hazardous operations
Experience with LOX/methane engine testing or cryogenic facilities
Familiarity with European space programs and standards (e.g. ECSS, ESA‑style reviews)
Experience with regulated industrial sites, permitting, or environmental compliance
Background in high‑cadence test operations
Ability to lead cross‑functional teams and make sound technical and operational decisions
Strong ownership and delivery mindset
Systems‑level thinking and interface management
Calm decision‑making during high‑pressure test activities
Strong documentation and reporting discipline
Fluent in English; French or German is a plus.

Serve as a senior technical advisor in physical sciences and engineering to evaluate the technical feasibility, maturity, and risks of proposed energy technologies and commercialization projects. Analyze technology-to-market programs to assess their effectiveness, identify performance barriers, and recommend strategic improvements.

Foster collaborative partnerships and coordinate initiatives among national laboratories, plants, sites, other federal and state agencies, and private-sector stakeholders. Degree: physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. OR B.

Combination of education and experience: education equivalent to one of the majors shown in A above that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

Specialized experience for this position is defined as meeting 2 of the following 3: Provide guidance on technology commercialization, lab-to-market funding programs, energy end-use sectors, or technology maturation processes that advance program objectives.

Act as a technical point of contact to build consensus among corporate partners, research facilities, academic institutions, Tribal organizations and DOE National Laboratories for all joint technology commercialization projects.

Assist with writing briefing materials or reports that are used by management to develop technical recommendations that advance technology commercialization objectives. "Experience" refers to paid and unpaid experience.

Als Complaints Manager bist du eine zentrale Anlaufstelle für unsere Kundinnen und Kunden und stellst sicher, dass ihre Anliegen professionell, effizient und kundenorientiert bearbeitet werden. Du nimmst Beschwerden entgegen, erfasst diese im System und stellst eine strukturierte Bearbeitung durch die zuständigen Facheinheiten sicher. Komplexere Fälle übernimmst du teilweise selbst, klärst diese funktionsübergreifend und sorgst für eine transparente sowie zeitgerechte Kommunikation gegenüber unseren Kundinnen und Kunden.

In dieser Rolle bist du Teil eines kleinen, engagierten Teams, das eigenverantwortlich und lösungsorientiert arbeitet. Dabei bringst du deine Erfahrung aktiv ein und trägst dazu bei, aus Kundenfeedback gezielt Verbesserungen abzuleiten.
**Das kannst du bewirken**
* Du nimmst Kundenbeschwerden entgegen, stellst eine strukturierte Triage sicher und koordinierst die effiziente Bearbeitung durch die zuständigen Facheinheiten
* Du bearbeitest komplexe Beschwerden eigenständig, führst interne Abklärungen durch und unterstützt aktiv bei der Erarbeitung nachhaltiger Lösungen
* Du arbeitest eng mit internen und externen Stakeholdern wie Rechtsdienst, Datenschutz, Unternehmenskommunikation sowie der Ombudsstelle für Privatversicherungen zusammen und stellst eine fristgerechte Fallbearbeitung sicher
* Du identifizierst wiederkehrende Problemfelder und gibst diese an das Customer Experience Team weiter, damit gezielte Verbesserungen für unsere Kundinnen und Kunden angestossen werden können
* Du verantwortest die Weiterentwicklung und Durchführung des E-Learnings für dezentrale Beschwerdemanagerinnen und -manager und unterstützt bei der Aufbereitung von Erkenntnissen, Handlungsempfehlungen und Präsentationen für unterschiedliche Stakeholder unter Einsatz moderner AI-gestützter Arbeitsmethoden
**Das bringst du mit**
* Abgeschlossene kaufmännische Ausbildung, idealerweise in der Versicherungsbranche; eine Weiterbildung (HF/FH) oder ein Bachelorabschluss in Betriebswirtschaft, Versicherungswirtschaft, Kommunikation oder Customer Experience ist von Vorteil
* Erfahrung im direkten Kundenkontakt, idealerweise im Beschwerdemanagement, sowie ausgeprägte Kommunikationsfähigkeiten in Wort und Schrift, insbesondere in anspruchsvollen oder konfliktreichen Situationen
* Hohe Service- und Lösungsorientierung sowie ein ausgeprägtes Mass an Eigenverantwortung, Zuverlässigkeit und Diskretion
* Strukturierte, selbstständige und sorgfältige Arbeitsweise sowie hohe Belastbarkeit und Freude daran, auch in anspruchsvollen Situationen den Überblick zu behalten
* Sehr gute MS-Office-Kenntnisse (PowerPoint, Excel, Word) sowie Erfahrung in der Nutzung von AI-Tools (u. a. Copilot)
* Sehr gute Französischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift; Italienischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil.

**Darum geht es bei Bosch: Um dich, unser Business, unsere Umwelt. **

## Rejoins notre équipe tipee ! ##
Situés au cœur de Lausanne, nous sommes une PME d'une cinquantaine de collaboratrices et collaborateurs passionné-e-s. Nous développons tipee, une application de gestion du temps et portail RH qui simplifie la vie de nos clients depuis plus de 10 ans.
Fonctionnant en mode participatif et agile, notre société est organisée en cercles où chacun-e est autonome, avec son mot à dire et des possibilités d'évolution au sein de la boîte. Et cela, avec un impact positif pour nos clients, nos collègues, la communauté et l'environnement.
Pour renforcer notre organisation, nous cherchons un-e **People & Culture Manager**. Ce poste de cadre te place au cœur de l'humain chez tipee : tu veilles à ce que chacun-e soit soutenu-e et accompagné-e au quotidien, tu fais vivre l'équité et la cohérence de nos pratiques RH, et tu contribues activement à notre culture d'entreprise et à notre marque employeur.
Ce poste combine deux rôles : à titre principal, celui de **People & Culture Manager**, et à titre secondaire, celui de **facilitateur-trice** au sein de nos cercles.
## Ton rôle au quotidien ##
Tu fais partie de la direction et tu travailles en lien étroit avec l'ensemble des cercles et des coordinateurs-trices.
* Tu es **à l'écoute des besoins** des collègues et des coordinateurs-trices, et tu es la personne de référence pour tout sujet touchant à l'humain au sein de tipee.
* Tu accompagnes les cercles dans leurs **recrutements** : tu ne recrutes pas à leur place, tu les outilles pour qu'ils sachent le faire eux-mêmes, et tu les appuies pour optimiser chaque processus.
* Tu conçois et fais vivre un **onboarding et un offboarding formalisés**, pour que chaque nouvel-le arrivant-e soit bien accueilli-e et chaque départ bien accompagné, quel que soit le cercle.
* Tu accompagnes l'évolution professionnelle des collaborateurs-trices : entretiens annuels en duo lorsque nécessaire, discussions avec les personnes concernées, et une réflexion continue sur les **parcours et la mobilité interne**.
* En collaboration avec les cadres, tu gères les **situations difficiles** (résolution de tensions, recadrage, conflit, etc.), avec la discrétion et l'écoute que ces moments demandent.
* Tu participes à la **diversité, l'équité et l'inclusion (DEIB)** au sein de tipee, et tu veilles à ce que nos pratiques soient inclusives à chaque étape du parcours collaborateur-trice.
* Tu clarifies et fais vivre **nos bonnes pratiques** : rédaction de guides, conventions et chartes en duo avec la direction, et contribution aux réflexions sur notre culture d'entreprise lors des séances cadres.
* Tu portes le rôle de **facilitateur-trice** : animation de rituels et stimulation de l'intelligence collective au sein de nos cercles.
* Tu participes à l'**organisation et à l'animation** de nos journées annuelles au vert.
* Tu t'assures que nos **cercles et rôles** suivent l'évolution de nos équipes.
* Tu **représentes tipee** à l'externe, lors de conférences ou salons RH, et tu partages ainsi notre vision de l'humain au travail.
* Tu favorises le **partage de connaissances** en interne et l'amélioration continue de nos pratiques, notamment via le suivi de notre questionnaire eNPS.
## Ce qu'on recherche ##
* Une expérience confirmée dans un rôle très orienté vers l'humain "- People & Culture, coaching, facilitation, Scrum Master, ou fonction similaire.
* Une posture de coach : tu préfères outiller et responsabiliser les équipes plutôt que de faire à leur place.
* Une réelle capacité d'écoute, d'empathie et de discrétion, notamment dans les situations sensibles.
* Un esprit d'initiative et l'envie de faire évoluer nos pratiques.
* Une aisance avec la culture produit, l'agilité et la facilitation (animation de rituels, intelligence collective, gestion des tensions).
* Le goût de représenter une entreprise à l'externe et de créer des partenariats.
* Une bonne compréhension du fonctionnement en cercles et en rôles, ou l'envie de t'y investir pleinement.
* De bonnes connaissances RH sont un plus, mais ne sont pas une condition.
Tu n'as pas besoin d'avoir un parcours RH classique pour réussir dans ce rôle : ce n'est pas un poste d'administration du personnel. Ce qui compte avant tout, c'est ta capacité à accompagner les gens, à faciliter, à créer de la confiance et être un soutien.
## Travailler chez tipee ##
* **Flexibilité** : horaires modulables, travail hybride (jusqu'à 50% à distance), taux d'activité adaptable à l'évolution de ta vie personnelle.
* **Locaux à Lausanne** : à 15 minutes à pied de la gare, ou 7 en vélo ou trottinette.
* **Formation** : un budget individuel pour des conférences ou formations sur les sujets qui t'intéressent.
* **Culture participative** : entraide, dialogue, confiance, prise de responsabilités.
* **Engagements** : certifiée B Corp et STI, engagée sur les aspects sociétaux et environnementaux.
* **Mobilité** : jusqu'à CHF 300.- par année pour tes frais de transport durable (abonnement CFF).
* **Conditions** : des prestations LPP attractives auprès d'une caisse durable, des avantages autour du congé parental, au moins 5 semaines de vacances, et plus.
* **Vie d'entreprise** : événements réguliers et moments conviviaux qui rythment l'année.

Our client is a large organisation based in Switzerland with an international and multicultural working environment
## Job Description ##
In this role, you will support the day-to-day management and improvement of HR policies, processes and practices.
You will review existing HR policies, procedures and guidelines and coordinate the necessary updates with HR colleagues and other internal stakeholders. This will involve working directly on documents, templates, forms and supporting materials to ensure they remain accurate, clear and easy to use.
You will help translate legal, regulatory and internal requirements into practical HR procedures.
You will follow relevant changes, identify which documents or processes need to be adapted and coordinate updates with the appropriate specialists.
A key part of the position will be process improvement.
You will review how existing HR processes work in practice, gather feedback from users, identify recurring issues and propose practical adjustments.
You will also use available data and KPIs to monitor processes and identify areas where efficiency or service quality can be improved.
You will work closely with different HR teams to support the implementation and consistent application of policies and procedures.
This may include answering questions, clarifying processes, preparing guidance and helping colleagues and managers understand how policies should be applied in practice.
You will coordinate a range of HR projects and improvement initiatives.
Your responsibilities will include preparing project plans, organising meetings and workshops, following up on actions, coordinating contributors, tracking deadlines and deliverables and ensuring that agreed changes are implemented.
You will organise and facilitate working sessions with relevant stakeholders to gather requirements, review existing practices and agree on practical solutions.
You will also support the rollout of new or updated HR policies and processes.
This includes coordinating validation, preparing implementation materials and working with communication colleagues to ensure that information is clear, accessible and available to the relevant audiences.
The position requires regular coordination with multiple stakeholders and the ability to manage several topics simultaneously while ensuring accurate follow-up and documentation.
## The Successful Applicant ##
We are looking for an experienced HR professional who enjoys working on concrete HR processes, policies and projects and who is comfortable moving between detailed documentation and stakeholder coordination.
You bring several years of HR experience, ideally within a large international organisation.
You have practical experience working with HR policies, procedures, process improvement and HR projects.
You hold a university degree or equivalent higher education qualification.
An additional HR qualification and familiarity with the Swiss employment and regulatory environment would be an advantage.
You are comfortable reviewing HR policies and procedures, understanding regulatory requirements and translating them into clear documentation and workable processes.
You have good project coordination skills and are used to managing actions, timelines, documentation and multiple stakeholders. You are comfortable organising meetings and workshops, following up on decisions and ensuring that agreed actions are completed.
You have a practical and solution-oriented approach.
You can identify gaps or inefficiencies in existing processes and suggest realistic improvements that make everyday HR activities simpler and more consistent.
Accuracy and attention to detail are important for this position.
You are comfortable working directly on policies, guidelines, templates, forms and process documentation and can ensure information remains consistent and up to date.
You communicate clearly and can work effectively with HR colleagues, managers and other internal stakeholders.
You are comfortable explaining processes, gathering feedback and coordinating different inputs to reach workable solutions.
Organised and autonomous, you can manage several activities at the same time, prioritise effectively and follow topics through to completion.
Fluency in French and English is required.
## What's on Offer ##
This is a varied and hands-on HR role where you will work directly on policies, processes, documentation and improvement projects.
You will have the opportunity to see the practical results of your work and contribute to making HR processes clearer and easier to use for employees, managers and HR teams.
You will join an international and collaborative working environment and interact with a broad range of HR specialists and internal stakeholders.
The position offers a good mix of operational HR work, project coordination and continuous improvement.
The organisation offers attractive employment conditions, flexibility, professional development opportunities and a supportive working environment.
The position is permanent and available at an 80-100% activity rate.
